hypothesis_and_rationale: Assumption: the broad thesis means an academically motivated machine learning strategy combining medium-term momentum, short-term reversal, and volatility. A regularized nonlinear model may predict relative returns by learning interactions between these effects. This is a testable hypothesis, not an established alpha. Assume comparable daily closing timestamps, positive prices adjusted for relevant corporate actions, a point-in-time asset universe, and permission to short. Closing prices alone cannot establish liquidity or borrow availability.
factor_formula: Let r(i,t)=ln(C(i,t)/C(i,t−1)). At close t, calculate eight features: 1-day and 5-day cumulative returns; momentum ln(C(i,t−5)/C(i,t−k)) for k∈{21,63,126,252}; and daily-return standard deviation over 21 and 63 days. Require 253 consecutive valid closes. Within each date's eligible universe, winsorize each feature at the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, then standardize to zero mean and unit variance; set constant features to zero. Construct φ from these eight standardized features, their squares, and all pairwise products. The training label for observation date s is the cross-sectionally standardized return ln(C(i,s+2)/C(i,s+1)). This delayed close-to-close label is a proxy for the intended next-open holding period. Fit ridge regression: minimize the average, across training dates, of each date's mean squared prediction error, plus λ||β||², with λ=1 and an unpenalized intercept. The factor is f(i,t)=b+βᵀφ(i,t). These model choices are fixed assumptions.
portfolio_weighting_rules: Refit after each month's final close using the latest 756 eligible observation dates, requiring at least 504. At refit cutoff T, include only labels with s+2≤T. Score assets daily after close t using the latest fitted model. Require at least 20 eligible assets; otherwise target cash. Set n=floor(N/5), long the n highest scores at +0.5/n each, and short the n lowest at −0.5/n each; all other weights are zero. Break ties by fixed asset identifier. This produces net exposure zero and gross exposure one. Submit these targets for execution at the next bar's open, allowing positions to remain unchanged until then. Assume fractional positions and fully funded margin without additional leverage. Missing-data exits occur at the next executable open; never retrospectively remove failed or delisted assets.
validation_plan: Use chronological walk-forward evaluation with monthly refitting and a final untouched 20% of dates. Keep feature definitions, λ, and portfolio rules fixed before that holdout; use earlier chronological folds for any proposed changes. At every cutoff, enforce label availability and reconstruct the universe using information known then. Compare against equal-weight momentum, reversal, and linear-only ridge portfolios under identical execution and costs. Measure daily rank correlation, net Sharpe, drawdown, turnover, concentration, and stability across assets and market periods. Test feature-group removals and nearby lookbacks to assess robustness. Apply transaction costs to absolute traded notional using hypothetical 5, 10, and 25 basis-point scenarios, plus explicit borrow-cost scenarios. Exact next-open returns require opening prices, which the specified input lacks: closing prices can generate all signals and targets, but any close-based performance calculation must be labeled a proxy. Obtain opening prices, execution costs, and borrow availability before validating tradable performance. Do not report proxy performance as an executable backtest or invent results.
